newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Aggressive buying firms mogas.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Aggressive buying firms mogas.

text.p: Gasoline prices recovered slightly to trade past the $24.00 per barrel mark amid aggressive buying while naphtha slipped with crude, traders said.
A Japanese trader emerged early in the day to bid at $23.95 per barrel for 95-octane unleaded gasoline loading in June, and improved his bid to buy 75,000-barrels offered by a Dutch trader at $24.10.
On Wednesday, unleaded 92-octane traded at $23.75 for June 15-20 lifting between the Dutch trader and another Japanese trader while the 95-octane was bid higher than the offer at $23.75/$23.45.
"It is fairly neutral," a trader said on Thursday's deal level.
Some traders discounted a draw in Singapore's weekly light distillates stocks in the week ending May 28.
Stocks which comprise gasoline, reformate and naphtha, fell by 653,000 barrels to 6.662 million barrels, easing from its two-year high at 7.6 million barrels just two weeks ago.
But traders said there still ample supplies.
"It still looks a bit on the long side with cargoes coming in from Australia, Thailand and South Korea," a trader with a major oil company said on June arrival cargoes.
A 200,000-barrel Mideast cargo was also heading to Singapore in the second-half of June, a source said.
Traders said they were looking to Taiwan's tender for July which closes June 4 and for prices in Asia to drop enough to open the arbitrage window to the U.S. to take out the length.
They also awaited results from India's July tender but news on the tender which closed on Wednesday was limited as they said their offices in Europe were handling the tender.
Naphtha June swaps slipped late on Thursday to $21.85/$22.00 per barrel, from $22.10/$22.20 on Wednesday.
July swaps were talked at par to June but slipped back into a 10-15 cent contango late Thursday.

Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) bought by tender 28,000-tonnes of July naphthenic and aromatic (N+A) naphtha at slightly above $215 per tonne c-and-f Kaohsiung, a company official said.
The level was much lower than CPC's last award, for May 11-31 delivery, at just below $230 per tonne, c-and-f.
The tender which sought the cargo for July 20-31 arrival, closed May 28 and was valid for two days.
(Prices are in dollars per barrel)
